programme.title: Eredivisie file
programme.desc: The fifth episode focuses on the free kick. A successful free kick is the ultimate proof that your feet can do what your head wants. But in the Eredivisie there is less and less room to cheer after a direct free kick. programme.title: Africa: hot life – Dry savanna | E01
programme.desc: Almost all wild inhabitants of hot regions of the world, such as Africa, are at risk of extinction due to climate change. The authors wonder whether and to what extent they will be able to adapt to new, difficult living conditions. Lions' prey tend to feed when the hunters are resting - the hottest time of the day. The increase in temperature affects the behavior of animals living in these hot areas. Great Britain. 2022. documentary series

programme.title: Ice Age: Frozen World | E02
programme.desc: Naturalist and explorer Steve Backshall and wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan take viewers on a gripping journey into the heart of the Ice Age. Using stunning outdoor photography from around the world and interviews with experts, they chronicle the rise of prehistoric megabeasts, from woolly mammoths to saber-toothed cats. They also present the history of the fight between Neanderthals and Homo sapiens. They will discover the secrets of the era that created the world we live in. It turns out that another extreme temperature drop on Earth may be caused by... climate change and global warming. The Ice Age became an arena of struggle between Neanderthals and representatives of Homo sapiens. Steve Backshall and Michaela Strachan investigate how two competing species have adapted to extreme conditions. Backshall explores southern Germany, where he discovers traces of the life of early humans and their ability to deal with prehistoric predators using advanced tools and weapons. In turn, Strachan examines the differences in anatomy and skills between Neanderthals and Homo sapiens. It turns out that despite the physical advantage of the former, the latter showed greater abilities in long-distance running and technological innovation. The key technology that gave them the advantage was the sewing needle, which allowed them to create tighter clothing. The decisive moment that led to the extinction of Neanderthals was global warming and environmental changes that left Homo sapiens as the dominant species. Great Britain. 2022. documentary film

programme.title: Planet of Sharks – Ocean Wanderer | S01E02
programme.desc: Scientists use modern technologies to monitor the underwater life of various species of sharks. These cartilaginous fish are completely unjustifiably associated with bloodthirsty predators. They hunt intelligently, using their keen senses and developed hunting instincts. Viewers will see, among others: how a whitetip shark senses the heartbeat of its prey. Sharks have lived on Earth since before the age of dinosaurs - they have been roaming the oceans for over 400 million years. Only today are scientists beginning to discover the secrets of their evolutionary success. USA. 2022. documentary series

programme.title: Big cats in a small world – Flood | E02
programme.desc: The life of the big cats living in the Gomoti River in Botswana is not an easy one. They have to deal with floods as well as intruders. Surviving in this demanding environment forces leopards, lions and cheetahs to use all their skills. The Moelo herd is very exhausted. Faced with winter flooding, young cheetahs must make a difficult decision. Sephiri must choose between her family and her young ones. Canada. 2024. documentary series

programme.desc: «The least expected day: Ep.1» The old guard receives the recording of a new season of the series with many cautions. However, the new generation sees it as an opportunity. programme.title: 30 for 30: One and Not Done
programme.desc: 30 for 30 (Sports). As part of its 30th anniversary celebration, ESPN looks back at notable sports happenings that occurred from 1979 to 2009 with this documentary series featuring 30 films from some of Hollywood's finest directors and producers. Peter Berg, Barry Levinson, John Singleton, Spike Jonze, Dan Klores, Barbara Kopple, Ron Shelton and Albert Maysles are among the filmmakers involved, and the stories told include the shocking trade of Wayne Gretzky in 1988, the Baltimore Colts' nighttime move in 1984, Reggie Miller's rivalry with the New York Knicks, the death of Len Bias in 1986, a profile of George Steinbrenner and his family business, and a look at Michael Jordan's attempt at a baseball career. A new series of 30 films premiered in October 2012 with «Broke,» about the challenges athletes face in managing their money

S1, Ep2 «Africa's Hunters»…For ten years Kamuti, a wise old leopard, has reigned over two square miles of prime hunting ground in the Luangwa Valley. She's held her own against the lions who steal her kills and survived to be thirteen years old, one of the oldest leopards in the African bush. programme.title: In the animal world. 1 p.

programme.desc: Its origin in the foothills of the Rockies is hardly known, but from there the huge Mississippi feeds a vast network of headwaters and tributaries. These run through the USA from the Rocky Mountains in the west to the Appalachian mountain range in the far east. After the water meets the Mississippi River, it flows south into the Gulf of Mexico. \n\nThis documentary by Simon Blakeney tells the story of this fascinating lifeline of the United States. The Mississippi is illuminated from all sides. The result is an elaborate BBC production with special recordings of the interaction between nature, wildlife and people.

programme.title: The largest rivers in the world
programme.desc:
Fascinating water world! Africa's fourth-longest river meanders over 2,574 kilometers from its source on the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo until it flows into the Indian Ocean in Mozambique. On the way there, you will be amazed by the gigantic Victoria Falls, which have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989. Here the mighty river falls at a width of 1,708 meters into a gorge approximately 110 meters deep. Until it flows into the Indian Ocean, the Zambezi crosses Angola, Zambia, forms borders with Namibia and Zimbabwe and ends in Mozambique. The people along its banks live with its rhythm: floods bring fertile soil and secure agriculture.

Further stages: Batoka Gorge and Lake Kariba. 

Last episode of the three-part series.

programme.title: Wild North Atlantic
programme.desc: This journey takes the underwater filmmaker into the barely explored world of the North Atlantic. Ken O'Sullivan is the first to document the migration routes of fin whales along the south coast of Ireland. (Station info).

programme.title: Heroes of evolution
programme.desc: Majestic whales, playful dolphins, curious seals and powerful polar bears: fascinating insights into the survival strategies of marine mammals. (Station info).

programme.title: Heroes of evolution
programme.desc: Sea and land turtles impress with their variety of shapes and their sophisticated adaptations. Their life between land, river and sea shows how resilient they are. (Station info).

programme.title: Heroes of evolution
programme.desc: Over 20 species of crocodiles, alligators and caimans live in 91 countries. Their behavior shows that there is more to teeth and scales than mere danger. (Station info).

programme.title: Heroes of evolution
programme.desc: Elephants roam the wild in Africa and Asia. Intelligence, memory and strength make them fascinating survivors. (Station info).

programme.title: Animal Park: Zoo Stories from Longleat
programme.desc: Is the breeding program for red squirrels about to end? Two of the endangered rodents cannot live together. Meanwhile, there are increasing signs of red pandas having offspring. (Station info).

programme.title: Animal Park: Zoo Stories from Longleat
programme.desc: Longleat's keepers face a difficult task: gaining the trust of baby koala Hazel. Meanwhile, the park's monitor lizard has to go to an osteopath. (Station info).

programme.title: Eden on Earth – The Last Paradise
